contents.name: §2.3.2 Positive Linear Functionals
contents.reason: This section develops order-cone positivity and positive extensions; the present pair uses unrestricted normed-space functionals and does not introduce an ordered vector-space structure.

contents.name: Definition 2.37 (Ordered Vector Space)
contents.reason: Its cone axioms are specific to the omitted positive-functional theory and do not enter the gauge, separation, annihilator, or complement arguments scaffolded here.

contents.name: Theorem 2.38 (Hahn--Banach for Positive Linear Functionals)
contents.reason: Positive domination by an ordered cone is a materially different extension theorem from the analytic Hahn--Banach prerequisite used in this geometric pair.

contents.name: Exercise 2.39 (direct Zorn proof of Theorem 2.38)
contents.reason: It is a second proof route for the excluded positive-extension theorem, rather than a lemma needed for the geometric Hahn--Banach route selected for this page.

contents.name: Exercise 2.40 (failure of positive extension without O3)
contents.reason: The counterexample concerns an order-theoretic axiom for positive functionals on continuous functions, which the present normed-space separation development never assumes.

contents.name: Exercise 2.42 (nonempty-interior hypothesis cannot be omitted)
contents.reason: Its two empty-interior ell-squared sets share a closure; the companion instead proves the directly relevant zero-distance obstruction to strong separation in an elementary plane example.

contents.name: Exercise 2.43 (dense difference of two closed convex ell-squared sets)
contents.reason: This stronger infinite-dimensional construction has no affine separator at all and requires its separate exercise argument; it is not needed to state the compactness hypothesis sharply.

contents.name: Lemma 2.44 (interior and closure of a convex set)
Lemma 2.45 (strict inequality on an interior passes to the closure)
Exercise 2.47 (affine hyperplanes are inverse images under nonzero bounded functionals)
Corollary 2.48 (open convex set disjoint from a subspace)
Corollary 2.49 (open convex set as intersection of open half-spaces)
Corollary 2.50 (strong separation of closed and compact convex sets)
Exercise 2.51 (a closed convex set is an intersection of closed half-spaces)
Theorem 2.53 (Hahn--Banach for a subspace and an exterior point)
Corollary 2.57 (duals of subspaces and quotient spaces)
contents.reason: The restriction and quotient-dual identifications require the full dual-space and quotient-factorisation setup, whose planned home treats those maps and their norms together.

contents.name: Corollary 2.58 (quotient-dual norm identities)
contents.reason: These exact norm equalities are consequences of the deferred restriction/quotient-dual identification and should be proved where the quotient-dual maps are formally defined.

contents.name: Exercise 2.60 (equivalent complement, projection, and right-inverse formulations)
Statement following Lemma 2.61 (Phillips: c-zero is not complemented in ell-infinity)

contents.name: Examples following the Minkowski functional (norm ball and a strip)
Examples following the Minkowski functional (a nonabsorbing line segment with infinite gauge)
Lemma 5.1 (gauge homogeneity, subadditivity, and open sublevel recovery)
Example after Theorem 5.3 (c-zero shows openness is essential)
contents.reason: This example concerns failure of separation when neither set supplies the required openness; the pair instead gives a closed-set zero-distance example tailored to strong separation.

contents.name: Corollary 5.4 (closed convex and compact sets are strongly separated)
Corollary 5.5 (open convex set and a subspace)
Problem 5.3 (polar and prepolar)
contents.reason: Polars require the dual pairing and a separate polar calculus; that structure belongs with adjoints and annihilators rather than this first separation treatment.

contents.name: Problem 5.4 (bipolar theorem)
contents.reason: The bipolar theorem is a global locally convex duality result; this pair supplies only the continuous-functional separation needed before weak topologies are formally built.

contents.name: Weak-star topology sigma(X*,X)
contents.reason: Weak-star neighbourhoods and their comparison with weak neighbourhoods need the full dual pairing and are deliberately deferred to the dedicated topology page.

contents.name: Theorem 5.10 (Banach--Alaoglu)
contents.reason: Weak-star compactness of the dual ball uses a product compactness construction absent from this local separation page and has a dedicated later home.

contents.name: Example after Theorem 5.11 (weak closure of the unit sphere)
contents.reason: The unit-sphere weak-closure phenomenon needs finite-codimensional weak neighbourhoods and is best developed once the weak topology, not just its local closure test, is available.

contents.name: Theorem 5.13 (Goldstine)
contents.reason: Goldstine concerns the weak-star density of the primal unit ball in the bidual and therefore requires bidual notation and weak-star topology beyond this pair.

sources.title: Piotr Hajlasz, Functional Analysis
sources.recovery_note: The Paperzz mirror was reported terminal-dead by the batch liveness sweep. This is the same Hajlasz course-note treatment at the author's University of Pittsburgh host, in its current 189-page edition; §10.5 renumbers the earlier mirror's complemented-subspace material but retains the Phillips proof and its almost-disjoint-family argument.
sources.locator: §10.5 “Complemented subspaces”, source PDF pp. 93--97 (printed pp. 94--98): from Theorem 10.11 through completion of the proof of Theorem 10.19 (Phillips), immediately before §11.

contents.name: Theorem 10.11 (topological direct sums and quotient identifications)
Remark 10.12 (the notation X = M direct-sum N denotes the identified Banach-space direct sum)
Proposition 10.13 (images of the two summands under a Banach-space isomorphism are complementary closed subspaces)
contents.reason: This transport-of-structure proposition is not used by the finite-dimensional, finite-codimensional, or Phillips routes on this pair; proving it would repeat the direct-sum machinery already published rather than advance a planned claim.

contents.name: Proposition 10.14 (closed Hilbert subspaces are complemented)
contents.reason: Orthogonal complementation is a Hilbert-space result requiring inner-product geometry; the present page treats the general normed-space finite-dimensional and finite-codimensional cases instead.

contents.name: Corollary 10.16 (a closed subspace is complemented iff it is the range of a projection)
Theorem 10.18 (Lindenstrauss--Tzafriri)
contents.reason: The characterization of Banach spaces with every closed subspace complemented is explicitly a difficult structural theorem and is far beyond this introductory geometric page.
